problem: Test whether shorter hours at the same pay could keep output while improving staff wellbeing.
title: 61 UK companies trial a four-day week with no pay cut
actor_name: 61 UK organisations (4 Day Week Campaign, Autonomy)
context: A coordinated six-month pilot ran from June to December 2022 with about 2,900 workers.
decision_made: Move to a four-day week at the same pay for six months.
action_taken: Researchers measured revenue, staff turnover and wellbeing during the trial.
observed_outcome: 56 of 61 companies (92 percent) continued the four-day week and 18 made it permanent. Revenue rose 1.4 percent on average and staff departures fell 57 percent. A one-year follow-up found at least 54 of the 61 still operating it.
lessons: Shorter weeks can hold revenue and cut turnover for organisations that choose to try them.
limitations: Companies opted in, so they may be unusually suited to it. The headline results come from the organisers' report, not an independent evaluation.

claims.claim_text: 61 UK companies trialled a four-day week from June to December 2022.
56 of the 61 companies planned to continue the four-day week after the pilot.
